desc:
Integration testing and error handling review shows what happens when the tools your app depends on slow down, fail or send odd answers. Ecom Swift LLC tests each connection, reports what breaks and improves the handling so one failure does not take down the screen.

## What is integration testing?

Integration testing checks the places where your app meets other software, such as a payment provider, an email service or a shipping tool. It does not ask whether your own code works alone. It asks whether the whole chain behaves when real messages travel across it.

A good test covers both the happy path and the unhappy ones: a slow reply, an empty answer, a rejected request or the same message arriving twice.

## Why the unhappy paths matter most

Most integrations work on the day they are built. Trouble arrives later, when a provider is slow for an hour, a customer enters an unexpected character or a webhook is delivered a second time. If your code never planned for these moments, it may crash, show a blank page or create a duplicate order.

Because these events are rare, they are rarely tested, and that is why they hurt. A single unhandled timeout can freeze checkout. A repeated message can charge or ship twice.

## How testing improves reliability and trust

Finding a weak spot before a customer does is the whole value. A test report lists each integration, what was tried and how your system responded. Issues are ranked by risk, so you fix the dangerous ones first.

Better error handling also changes how problems feel. Instead of a broken page, the visitor sees a short, friendly message and a way to try again. Staff see a clear log entry instead of a mystery. The result is calmer support and fewer lost transactions, since failures are contained instead of spreading.

## What a thorough test pass covers

- A written list of every integration and what each one does.
- Normal cases with typical data from each tool.
- Timeouts, slow replies and unreachable services.
- Empty, partial and malformed responses.
- Duplicate and out-of-order messages.
- Expired or revoked keys and permission errors.
- Retry behavior, to confirm retries stop instead of looping forever.
- Friendly messages shown to customers when a service fails.
- A ranked list of issues, with a re-test after the fixes.

## How we run it

We start by mapping your connections and agreeing which ones carry the most risk. Then we test in sandbox or test modes, so no real charges, emails or shipments are created. For each case we record what the system did and what it should have done.

The Basic package tests your most important integrations and reports. Standard adds fixes for the most serious handling problems and a re-test. Premium adds automated tests inside your project that run on every update, so the checking continues after we leave. If we find many problems, we rank them and agree with you which to fix first.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Test in sandbox modes provided by the other tools.
- Include failure cases in every test list.
- Show customers a clear message when a service is down.
- Make repeated messages safe to process twice.
- Re-run the tests after any provider update.

**Avoid:**
- Testing only with perfect sample data.
- Using live customer records for experiments.
- Retrying a failed call endlessly without a limit.
- Hiding errors from your own team.
- Treating a passing test today as proof for next year.

## Who it is for

A shop owner about to run a big campaign wants proof that checkout survives a slow payment response. A software team that has grown past manual clicking needs automated checks. A business that inherited a system from another developer wants a clear picture of where it is fragile.

## What we need from you

Send a list of the tools your app connects to, test or sandbox credentials where they exist, and access to the code or staging site. We work as a developer or collaborator user and never ask for passwords. Please do not give us live payment keys for testing, because sandbox keys are safer and cause no real charges.
